input: Research local Montessori preschool enrollment timelines

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether this covers one specific school or all local Montessori options determines how broad or narrow the research needs to be.
The child's current age and target start date directly affect which enrollment cycles and age-eligibility windows are relevant.
The specific city or neighborhood defines which schools are actually 'local' and reachable for this family.
Budget limits (e.g., tuition range, need for financial aid or subsidies) may rule out certain schools entirely, focusing research only on affordable options.
Whether the family prefers a pure AMI/AMS-accredited Montessori program vs. a Montessori-inspired one changes which schools qualify.
Knowing what a useful output looks like — a simple list of deadlines, a comparison table, a ready-to-send inquiry — shapes how the research is compiled and delivered.
Whether the user wants to do online research themselves, make phone calls, or have a structured checklist determines the immediate next action and tools needed.

gold.taskTitle: Research Montessori preschool enrollment timelines locally
gold.taskDescription: Find out when and how to enroll a child in a local Montessori preschool by researching key dates, processes, and requirements.

questions.title: Which specific city or neighborhood are you searching in?
questions.description: Identify the geographic area to define which schools count as 'local' for this research.

questions.title: How old is your child, and when should they start?
questions.description: Determine the child's current age and intended enrollment term to match the right enrollment cycle and age-eligibility cutoffs.

questions.title: Are you researching one school or all local options?
questions.description: Clarify whether the task is scoped to a single school already in mind or is a broader survey of every nearby Montessori program.

questions.title: Do you require AMI or AMS accreditation, or is Montessori-inspired acceptable?
questions.description: Establish the certification standard so only qualifying schools are included in the research.

questions.title: Is there a tuition budget or need for financial aid programs?
questions.description: Identify any hard cost limits or subsidy requirements that would eliminate certain schools from consideration.

questions.title: What should the final output of this research look like?
questions.description: Define what 'done well' means — a deadline checklist, a side-by-side school comparison, direct school contact details, etc.

questions.title: Will you research online, call schools directly, or need a checklist?
questions.description: Determine the preferred method and tools for conducting the research so the immediate next step is clear and actionable.
